items.stem: What was the Selma to Montgomery March?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué fue la Marcha de Selma a Montgomery?

choices.text: Four college students sat at a segregated Woolworth lunch counter
choices.textEs: Una marcha de celebración después de que se firmó la Ley de Derechos Civiles

choices.text: A voting rights march where marchers were beaten on Bloody Sunday
choices.textEs: Una marcha por derechos de voto donde marchistas fueron golpeados el Domingo Sangriento

choices.text: Poll taxes, literacy tests, grandfather clauses, and intimidation
choices.textEs: La primera manifestación organizada de derechos civiles en Alabama

choices.text: SCLC protests using children marchers that faced violent response
choices.textEs: Una marcha liderada por estudiantes protestando políticas de segregación escolar

items.explanation: The Selma to Montgomery marches were voting-rights demonstrations in 1965, and the first march became known as Bloody Sunday when troopers attacked protesters on the Edmund Pettus Bridge. Choices about bus integration are wrong because Selma focused on the right to vote. The violence helped build support for the Voting Rights Act.
